commits.message:
docs(contributing): recommend a blobless clone, and guard against a repeat

Cloning this repository transfers 252MB, but the working tree at HEAD is 1.1MB
across 152 files. Over 99% of the download is history: build artefacts were
committed early on and removed later, and .gitignore does not retract what is
already in history.

  soroban_cost_lints/test_fixtures/**/target/    932.6 MB of blobs
  target/debug/                                  640.6 MB of blobs
  all actual source                              ~10 MB

The largest single blob is a 36.1MB libstellar_xdr rlib, committed twice. The
files were added around #281 and removed in #328, so they are absent from the
tree yet still paid for on every clone.

Document `--filter=blob:none` in the six places a clone is described. A blobless
clone keeps the complete history and every branch, fetching file contents on
demand:

  plain clone            252 MB    minutes    full history
  --depth 1              432 KB    2.1 s      1 commit
  --filter=blob:none     1.1 MB    4.8 s      full history (351 commits)

Nothing prevented the artefacts being committed in the first place — there is no
pre-commit config and no size check in CI — so add a repo-hygiene job that fails
on any tracked path under target/ or any tracked file over 5MB. The largest
legitimate tracked file is ~108KB, so that threshold has wide headroom. It is
aggregated into build-and-test rather than exposed separately, to keep a single
required status context.

A history rewrite would take the repository to ~10MB permanently, but it would
break all 68 forks and invalidate commit SHAs cited across open issues, so it is
deliberately not attempted here.
